questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), the Supreme Court upheld 27% OBC reservation and capped total reservations, as a general rule, at:
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission case fixed the 50% ceiling, allowing breach only in extraordinary situations, and introduced the creamy layer exclusion.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Federalism and secularism were held to be basic features, and limits on the misuse of Article 356 were laid down, in:

options.A: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)
options.C: Shamsher Singh v. State of Punjab (1974)

questions.explanation: Bommai made a Presidential Proclamation under Article 356 subject to judicial review.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Besides enforcement of Fundamental Rights, High Courts may issue writs under Article 226 for:
questions.explanation: Article 226 is wider than Article 32 because High Courts can issue writs 'for any other purpose', i.e. to enforce legal rights.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The Ninety-ninth Constitutional Amendment and the NJAC Act were struck down in:

options.A: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
options.B: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015)
options.C: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (1993)
options.D: Union of India v. Sankalchand Himatlal Sheth (1977)

questions.explanation: The Fourth Judges Case held that the NJAC violated judicial independence, a basic feature, and restored the collegium.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: A 'Money Bill' is defined in which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 110 defines Money Bill; Article 109 prescribes the special procedure in Rajya Sabha.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: An ordinance promulgated under Article 123 ceases to operate at the expiry of how long after Parliament reassembles?
questions.explanation: It also lapses earlier if both Houses disapprove it by resolution.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The right to speedy trial was read into Article 21 in:

options.B: Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar
options.C: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
options.D: Francis Coralie Mullin v. Administrator, Delhi

questions.explanation: The case on undertrial prisoners in Bihar held that a speedy trial is an essential part of the fair procedure required by Article 21.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The 'essential religious practices' test under Article 25 originated in:
questions.explanation: The Shirur Mutt case (1954) held that the Constitution protects practices integral to a religion.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment inserted a new Part IX in the Constitution dealing with:
questions.explanation: Part IX (Articles 243–243O) provides for Panchayati Raj; municipalities are in Part IXA through the 74th Amendment.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers is provided for in:
questions.explanation: Article 262 empowers Parliament to provide by law for adjudication of inter-State water disputes and to bar court jurisdiction over them.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: Disqualification of legislators on the ground of defection is governed by the:
questions.explanation: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the Tenth Schedule; Kihoto Hollohan upheld its validity.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: The GST Council was constituted under which Article, inserted by the 101st Amendment?
questions.explanation: Article 279A provides for the Goods and Services Tax Council.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question: After the 44th Constitutional Amendment, the right to property is:

options.C: A statutory right under the Transfer of Property Act

questions.explanation: Article 31 and Article 19(1)(f) were repealed; Article 300A states no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: 'Law is the body of principles recognised and applied by the State in the administration of justice' is the definition given by:
questions.explanation: Salmond's definition is a conception of law based on its function in courts.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The utilitarian principle of 'the greatest happiness of the greatest number' is chiefly associated with:
questions.explanation: Bentham made utility the test of law and morality.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The 'inner morality of law', consisting of eight desiderata, was propounded by:
questions.explanation: In The Morality of Law, Fuller listed generality, publicity, non-retroactivity, clarity and similar requirements for a legal system.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: 'Law as integrity' and the view of rights as 'trumps' are associated with:
questions.explanation: Dworkin criticised legal positivism in Taking Rights Seriously and Law's Empire.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: The realist view that law is a prediction of what courts will do in fact is associated with:
questions.explanation: Holmes advanced this view in 'The Path of the Law' (1897).

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: A right available against the world at large is called:
questions.explanation: Rights in rem (such as ownership) bind everyone, while rights in personam bind specific persons.

questions.subject: Jurisprudence
questions.question: Under Article 141, the law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on:

options.A: All courts within the territory of India
options.B: Only the High Courts in India
options.C: Only courts hearing the same parties
options.D: Only subordinate courts of a State

questions.explanation: Article 141 gives the doctrine of precedent a constitutional footing in India.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Which of the following does NOT vitiate free consent under Section 14 of the Indian Contract Act?
questions.explanation: Section 14 lists coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation and mistake; inadequacy of consideration does not affect validity (Section 25 Explanation 2).

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Under Section 2(d) of the Indian Contract Act, consideration may move from:

options.A: Only the promisor before the contract
options.B: Only the promisee, never a third party
options.C: The promisee or any other person
options.D: A stranger to the contract alone

questions.explanation: Unlike English law, Indian law does not require that consideration move from the promisee.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: The doctrine of privity of contract means that:

options.A: A contract binds only the promisor
options.D: A stranger to a contract cannot sue upon it

questions.explanation: Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre Co. v. Selfridge affirmed that only parties can enforce a contract, subject to exceptions such as trusts and family arrangements.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: After the 2018 amendment to the Specific Relief Act, 1963, specific performance of a contract is:

options.B: A general remedy courts must ordinarily grant

questions.explanation: The amendment replaced the earlier discretionary approach in Section 10 and made specific performance the rule, with exceptions.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: Section 70 of the Indian Contract Act deals with:

options.A: Rights of a finder of lost goods
options.C: Compensation for loss caused by breach

questions.explanation: Section 70 embodies the principle of quantum meruit and restitution.

questions.subject: Law of Contract
questions.question: In Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya, the Supreme Court held that agreements collateral to wagering agreements are:

options.C: Void like the wagering agreement itself

questions.explanation: Section 30 declares only wagers void; collateral transactions are not hit by it, unless unlawful under other law.

questions.subject: Sale of Goods
questions.question: In an 'agreement to sell' under the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, the transfer of property in goods takes place:

options.A: Immediately on making the agreement, even before delivery
options.B: Only when the buyer resells the goods
options.C: At a future time or on a condition being fulfilled
options.D: Only on payment of the price in full

questions.explanation: In a completed 'sale' the property passes at once; an agreement to sell creates only a right to damages for breach until property passes.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: 'Injuria sine damno' means:

options.A: Injury suffered with the victim's consent
options.B: Harm caused by an unavoidable accident
options.C: Actual loss without violation of a legal right
options.D: Violation of a legal right without actual loss

questions.explanation: Ashby v. White held that infringement of a legal right is actionable per se.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: The maxim 'res ipsa loquitur' means:

options.C: Let the master answer for it

questions.explanation: It allows negligence to be inferred from the facts, as in Byrne v. Boadle.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: For criminal liability of doctors for medical negligence, Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab requires:
questions.explanation: The Court held mere negligence is not enough for criminal liability; gross negligence or recklessness is required.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: Under modern law, contributory negligence of the plaintiff ordinarily results in:

options.A: A complete bar to any recovery
options.C: Transfer of liability to a third party

questions.explanation: Apportionment replaced the harsh common-law rule in Butterfield v. Forrester that barred recovery.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: State immunity in tort for acts done in exercise of sovereign powers was recognised in India in:

options.A: Nilabati Behera v. State of Orissa
options.B: Rudul Sah v. State of Bihar
options.D: Kasturi Lal v. State of U.P.

questions.explanation: Kasturi Lal (1965) distinguished sovereign and non-sovereign functions; later cases confined the immunity, especially for fundamental rights violations.

questions.subject: Law of Torts
questions.question: In The Wagon Mound (No. 1), the test for remoteness of damage was held to be:

options.D: Market value of the property that was harmed

questions.explanation: The Privy Council replaced the direct-consequence test of Re Polemis with reasonable foreseeability.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The 'rarest of rare' doctrine for imposing the death penalty was laid down in:

options.A: Jagmohan Singh v. State of U.P. (1973)
options.B: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980)
options.D: Rajendra Prasad v. State of U.P. (1979)

questions.explanation: A Constitution Bench upheld the death penalty but restricted it to the rarest of rare cases, requiring special reasons.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Section 3(5) of the BNS, 2023 (earlier Section 34 IPC) deals with:

options.B: Offences by members of an unlawful assembly
options.C: Acts done jointly with common intention
options.D: Abetment of an offence to the public

questions.explanation: Section 3(5) fixes joint liability for criminal acts done in furtherance of the common intention of all.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Dowry death is dealt with in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 80 BNS corresponds to Section 304B IPC; Section 85 deals with cruelty by a husband or his relatives.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The offence of rape is defined in which section of the BNS, 2023?
questions.explanation: Section 63 corresponds to Section 375 IPC; Section 64 prescribes punishment.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Murder by a group of five or more persons acting in concert on grounds such as race, caste or community is punishable under the BNS with:

options.A: Imprisonment up to ten years and fine
options.C: Death or life imprisonment, and fine
options.D: Imprisonment up to seven years only

questions.explanation: Section 103(2) BNS creates this new aggravated form of murder (mob lynching).

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: Culpable homicide amounts to murder when the act is done with:

options.D: Knowledge that death is merely possible

questions.explanation: Intention to cause death is the first limb of murder; provocation reduces murder to culpable homicide.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The defence of unsoundness of mind in criminal law is based on:

options.C: The rule in R v. Dudley and Stephens

questions.explanation: The M'Naghten Rules (1843) require that the accused did not know the nature of the act or that it was wrong.

questions.subject: Criminal Law
questions.question: The right of private defence of the body extends to voluntarily causing death where there is a reasonable apprehension of:
questions.explanation: Death may be caused in defence only in the situations specifically enumerated, such as death, grievous hurt and rape.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 80 of the CPC, notice before filing a suit against the Government must be given at least:
questions.explanation: Section 80 requires two months' notice, though urgent relief may be sought with the court's leave.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A second appeal under Section 100 of the CPC lies only on:

options.A: Any question of fact or law

questions.explanation: The High Court must formulate the substantial question of law before hearing a second appeal.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: A plaint is liable to be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 of the CPC where it:

options.A: Is signed by an authorised advocate
options.B: Does not disclose a cause of action

questions.explanation: Rejection also follows if relief is undervalued, insufficiently stamped, or barred by law.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 151 of the CPC saves the inherent powers of the court to:

options.A: Enlarge the limitation period for suits
options.C: Hear appeals against its own decree
options.D: Make orders necessary for the ends of justice

questions.explanation: Inherent powers cannot be used to override express provisions of the Code.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 permits condonation of delay for:

options.C: Plaints, but not appeals or applications
options.D: Appeals and applications, but not suits

questions.explanation: Section 5 covers appeals and applications, but not suits.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: Under Section 187 of the BNSS, 2023, an accused gets default bail if investigation of an offence punishable with death or life imprisonment is not completed in:
questions.explanation: The 90-day period applies to offences punishable with death, life or imprisonment of ten years or more; 60 days for others.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: The Supreme Court laid down eleven requirements to be followed in all cases of arrest and detention in:

options.B: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
options.C: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
options.D: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India

questions.explanation: D.K. Basu (1997) laid down safeguards to prevent custodial torture.

questions.subject: Procedural Law
questions.question: The three essential conditions for grant of a temporary injunction are:

options.A: Notice to defendant, hearing and written arguments
options.B: Jurisdiction, pecuniary valuation, territorial limit and court fee
options.C: Locus standi, cause of action, limitation and costs
options.D: Prima facie case, balance of convenience, irreparable injury

questions.explanation: These tests are applied under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of the CPC.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Hearsay evidence is, as a general rule:

options.B: Admissible if the witness is a public servant

questions.explanation: Exceptions include res gestae, dying declarations and admissions.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: The rule of estoppel by representation prevents a person from:

options.A: Claiming costs on withdrawal of the suit by him
options.B: Calling any witness at the trial of the case
options.C: Denying what he led another to believe
options.D: Filing a second appeal against a decree

questions.explanation: Section 115 of the Evidence Act (Section 121 BSA) bars denial of a representation intentionally made and relied upon.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Admissibility of secondary electronic records, as held in Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer, requires:

options.B: Prior permission of the High Court
options.C: A notarised copy of the device invoice
options.D: An affidavit from the opposite party

questions.explanation: Under the BSA, 2023, the corresponding requirement is in Section 63.

questions.subject: Law of Evidence
questions.question: Conviction on the uncorroborated testimony of an accomplice is:

options.A: Permitted only in cases of offences against the State
options.B: Legally possible, but corroboration is prudent

questions.explanation: Section 133 makes an accomplice a competent witness; Section 114 illustration (b) cautions against reliance without corroboration.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a criterion of statehood under the Montevideo Convention, 1933?

options.A: Capacity to enter into relations with other States

questions.explanation: The criteria are population, territory, government and capacity to enter relations; UN membership is not a condition.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The 'Lotus principle' holds that States may act:

options.A: Only with prior authorisation of the Security Council
options.B: Unless a prohibitive rule of international law exists
options.C: Only where a treaty or convention expressly permits it
options.D: Only within their own territorial waters

questions.explanation: In the S.S. Lotus case (1927), the PCIJ said restrictions on State independence cannot be presumed.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The requirement of a 'genuine link' for diplomatic protection of nationals arose in:
questions.explanation: The ICJ held that Liechtenstein could not espouse Nottebohm's claim since his nationality lacked a genuine connection.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Formation of customary international law requires State practice and:
questions.explanation: The North Sea Continental Shelf cases stressed that practice must be accompanied by a belief that it is legally obligatory.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: Which of the following is outside the subject-matter jurisdiction of the ICC under the Rome Statute?
questions.explanation: The ICC tries genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and the crime of aggression.

questions.subject: International Law
questions.question: The principle of non-refoulement prohibits:

options.A: Returning a refugee to a place of persecution
options.B: Granting diplomatic immunity to every refugee
options.C: Expelling a foreign ambassador at will
options.D: Recognising a State before it is formed

questions.explanation: It is enshrined in Article 33 of the 1951 Refugee Convention and is widely regarded as customary law.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: Judicial separation under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is provided in Section:
questions.explanation: Section 9 deals with restitution of conjugal rights and Section 11 with void marriages.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: The iddat period of a divorced Muslim woman subject to menstruation is:
questions.explanation: Four months and ten days applies to a widow; for divorced women it is three menstrual courses.

questions.subject: Family Law
questions.question: In Gita Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India, the word 'after' in Section 6(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act was read as:
questions.explanation: The Court held that the mother can act as natural guardian even during the father's lifetime if he is absent from the minor's care.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: Under the doctrine of lis pendens (Section 52, TPA), a transfer of the disputed property during the suit:

options.A: Requires prior permission of the trial court
options.B: Remains subject to the outcome of the suit

questions.explanation: The transferee is bound by the decree passed in the pending suit.

questions.subject: Property Law
questions.question: The doctrine of part performance (Section 53A, TPA) protects:

options.A: A mortgagee who has not advanced the mortgage money
options.B: An agent who signed the deed on behalf of the principal
options.C: A tenant holding over after the lease expires
options.D: A transferee in possession under a written contract

questions.explanation: It is a shield and not a sword; the transferee can resist the transferor's claim for possession.

questions.subject: Succession Law
questions.question: A will is said to be 'ambulatory', which means that it:

options.A: Binds the executors during the testator's life
options.C: Can be revoked by the testator before his death
options.D: Must be registered to be valid

questions.explanation: A will takes effect only after the testator's death and may be changed at any time.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: The Novartis AG v. Union of India (2013) decision interpreted Section 3(d) of the Patents Act regarding:

options.A: Damages for infringement of pharmaceutical patents
options.D: Patentability of new forms of known substances

questions.explanation: The Court held that a new form of a known substance must show enhanced therapeutic efficacy.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: The first product registered as a Geographical Indication in India was:
questions.explanation: Darjeeling Tea was registered in 2004–05 under the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999.

questions.subject: Intellectual Property Law
questions.question: The 'special rights' of an author under Section 57 of the Copyright Act, 1957 are known as:
questions.explanation: Moral rights include the right to claim authorship and to restrain distortion of the work.

questions.subject: Environmental Law
questions.question: The precautionary principle was held to be part of Indian environmental law in:

options.A: Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra v. State of U.P.
options.B: Subhash Kumar v. State of Bihar
options.C: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
options.D: Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India

questions.explanation: Vellore (1996) also applied sustainable development and the polluter pays principle.

questions.subject: Environmental Law
questions.question: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted to give effect to decisions of the:

options.C: 1992 Rio Conference on Environment and Development

questions.explanation: Parliament enacted it under Article 253 to implement international decisions.

questions.subject: Company Law
questions.question: The doctrine of indoor management protects:

options.C: Persons dealing in good faith with a company

questions.explanation: Royal British Bank v. Turquand held that outsiders may assume that internal procedures have been complied with.

questions.subject: Administrative Law
questions.question: 'Wednesbury unreasonableness' is established where a decision is:

options.A: Contrary to the political interests of the ruling party
options.B: Made without hearing a formal appeal
options.C: So unreasonable no reasonable authority could make it
options.D: Delayed beyond the period in the statute

questions.explanation: Associated Provincial Picture Houses v. Wednesbury Corporation (1948) set a high threshold for judicial review on reasonableness.

questions.subject: Right to Information
questions.question: Under the RTI Act, 2005, information concerning life or liberty of a person must be provided within:
questions.explanation: The general period is thirty days; Section 7(1) requires forty-eight hours for life or liberty matters.

questions.subject: Arbitration Law
questions.question: Section 16 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 empowers the arbitral tribunal to:

options.A: Transfer the dispute to a civil court
options.D: Execute its award as a decree

questions.explanation: This is the principle of competence-competence (Kompetenz-Kompetenz), including objections to the arbitration agreement.

questions.subject: Information Technology Law
questions.question: Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the individual to whom personal data relates is called a:
questions.explanation: A Data Fiduciary determines the purpose and means of processing; the Data Principal is the individual.
